hero.headline: Hobe Sound getting first Aldi grocery store at former Winn-Dixie location
hero.body:
Hobe Sound is getting its first Aldi grocery store when the discount grocer opens July 9 at 8867 SE Bridge Road. The new store will occupy the space where Winn-Dixie previously operated.

Aldi has converted multiple Winn-Dixie stores across South Florida over the past few years. The company will hold a grand opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony on July 9 at 8:30 a.m.

The first 200 customers will receive a gift bag with Aldi products and a gift card. The Hobe Sound Aldi will be open daily from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m.

The new grocery store adds another retail option for Hobe Sound residents in northern Martin County. Aldi is known for its smaller store format and focus on private-label products at lower prices than traditional supermarkets.

cards.headline: Four Arrested After Armed Robbery and Pursuit in Martin County
cards.teaser: Four suspects were arrested following an armed robbery of a teenager and subsequent pursuit in Martin County, according to deputies.
cards.body:
Four suspects were arrested following an armed robbery of a teenager and subsequent pursuit in Martin County, according to deputies. The arrests came after Martin County deputies pursued the suspects.

The four individuals are accused in the armed robbery of a teen. Details about where the robbery occurred in Martin County were provided by the Martin County Sheriff's Office.

The pursuit ended with all four suspects in custody. The Martin County Sheriff's Office handled the investigation and arrests.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds skips Florida GOP governor debate as rivals invoke his name 60 times
cards.body:
Florida's first major Republican debate for governor took place Thursday night without its frontrunner. U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, backed by former President Trump, declined to appear alongside former House Speaker Paul Renner, Lt. Jay Collins, and businessman James Fishback. The three candidates mentioned Donalds by name at least 60 times during the two-hour event.

Moderator Patrick Bet-David opened by calling Donalds the elephant not in the room. Bet-David said he urged Donalds to attend, but Donalds responded that he has raised roughly $100 million and is polling between 48% and 58%. Donalds said he would only consider debating once another candidate reaches double digits in polling. Collins criticized the absence, saying the United States does not do kings and that Florida does not either. He added that if Donalds wants the governor's mansion, he has to grow a spine, stand up, and fight for the people of Florida. Renner called the decision disrespectful and argued every voter deserves a debate. Renner said Donalds is avoiding the stage because he cannot prove he is better qualified. Fishback contrasted Donalds' fundraising with his own ground game, noting his campaign became the first for Florida governor to visit all 67 counties. Donalds told WPLG previously that if the race was close, he would be debating.

The debate centered on property taxes, insurance, affordability, and hyperscale data centers. All are issues the candidates used to argue they would carry forward Gov. Ron DeSantis' conservative tenure. Fishback pledged to completely and totally abolish property taxes in Florida and promised to take a chainsaw to local government spending. Collins said cities and counties have a spending problem and need more accountability. Renner said the current property tax amendment does not go far enough and pitched his Florida First plan to eliminate most homestead property taxes while shifting more burden to tourists, out-of-state investors, and large corporations. The sharpest clash came over data centers. Fishback promised to reject and remove every experimental data center in Florida. Renner said he would call a special session to stop hyperscale projects. Collins urged local control with state guardrails, prompting Fishback to mock his answer as a word salad.

Renner leaned on his record as House Speaker, Collins emphasized his military service and role in the DeSantis administration, and Fishback positioned himself as an outsider. All three attacked Donalds while also making the case against each other. With Donalds still holding polling, fundraising, and endorsement advantages, the debate gave his rivals clips and contrasts but appeared unlikely to reset the race on its own.

cards.headline: Four suspects arrested after armed robbery pursuit in Martin County
cards.teaser: Four people accused in an armed robbery of a teenager were arrested following a pursuit in Martin County, according to deputies.
cards.body:
Martin County deputies arrested four people accused in an armed robbery of a teenager. The arrests came after a pursuit in Martin County.

Deputies reported the suspects were involved in robbing a teen. The incident led to a vehicle pursuit that ended with the apprehension of all four suspects.

Martin County Sheriff's Office conducted the investigation and arrests. The suspects face charges related to the armed robbery.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with global artist program
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is drawing local and international artists to Fort Pierce's Peacock Arts District, preserving the historic Crain Estate while offering tours and art classes.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation operates from the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain who once called the property home. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The foundation has kept the estate 90% the way it was when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with its manly paneling and stained glass. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting items for their Florida estate including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks in its design. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven birds that have since multiplied to over 100. Among the flock is Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognizable by his limp. Bob lives inside the estate, has his own bowls, and is hand-fed every day. The foundation runs an artist-in-residency program that attracts artists from around the world with simple but elegant accommodations on the property. Art director Krystal Masters leads the art lab, which offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels. The majority of Masters' classes are one-on-one where students come in with zero experience and walk out with a piece of art.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to right knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old Serena was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. She posted on Instagram that she was heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles, saying coming back to compete again has been a gift and the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to her. She said she did everything she could but unfortunately her knee just was not ready to compete.

The Instagram post included images of four syringes that Serena said shows the fluid they drained from my knee after my singles match. An accompanying video showed her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match that was not scheduled earlier in the week, having been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. Venus, who is 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde scare 3-2 in extra time to advance to World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and defending World Cup champion Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 Friday in South Florida, advancing to face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday after the tiny island nation challenged them until the final minutes of extra time.
cards.body:
Argentina's go-ahead score was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Messi scored in the 29th minute for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense on a well-timed run as Lisandro Martinez lofted a pass toward him. Messi took a quick touch and hammered a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha for a 1-0 lead. Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored for Cape Verde, both equalizers that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. Vozinha had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Cape Verde's memorable World Cup debut had been a stunning run, with the 40-year-old goalkeeper leading the team to surprising draws against Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia to become the smallest country to reach the knockout round.

Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappe in the Golden Boot race as the top scorer. He extended his World Cup record with 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak, moving two goals ahead of Mbappe on the all-time list.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football sets sights on state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for the 2026 fall season with a state title as their goal after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district title. A second-round playoff exit left the team feeling more was within reach. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year players, with the majority coming from the middle school program, so they know how things are run and have experienced significant success in their careers. Robertson expressed hope that their senior year will be the best season the program has had. The veteran senior class is leading the way as the program embraces a more demanding schedule this fall. Senior Jack Williams said the team wanted to take the program to the next level by creating a challenging schedule that allows them to compete against really good teams and attract new people.

For the Scots, improvement this season is measured by advancing further in the postseason. Senior Jack Whelche said a better year means going farther in the playoffs, noting that while the team wants to go undefeated in the season, that does not matter if they keep losing in the second round. The team must advance beyond that point. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the summer workouts add up every day as something to look forward to, with players working harder so they can see positive results when the season begins and break their record.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
Under The Sun Promotions, Inc announced the 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach in November 2026. The annual event has become a staple for Indian River County residents and visitors seeking local seafood and entertainment.

The festival will feature seafood vendors, live music, and family activities at its Vero Beach location. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc serves as the official organizer for the multi-day event that draws thousands of attendees each year.

The Treasure Coast Seafood Festival has grown into one of the region's most popular culinary events since its inception. The festival showcases fresh seafood from local waters and vendors from across Florida.

Under The Sun Promotions, Inc will release specific dates, ticket prices, and vendor information in the coming weeks. The festival typically runs over a weekend in November at Riverside Park in Vero Beach.
